text:
anika: Heads-up: planning a coordinated base-image rebuild and runtime hardening next Tue (03:00–06:00 UTC). Primary goals: drop unnecessary packages, enable rootless runtime bits, rotate the service-account creds used by the image-signer, and migrate signing to the new KMS-wrapped signer. Will affect Dedicated and Private clusters.

sam: +1. What are the RBAC changes you need? will this touch workload identities?

anika: We'll create a new k8s SA `image-signer` with a narrowed set of permissions. Quick draft: 
```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata: 
  name: image-signer-role
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
```
And bind only to `image-signer` SA in the infra namespace. We'll also add a short-lived RoleBinding for the canary runner.

liam: FYI the new KMS signer requires key-encrypt-wrap (KEK) support — ops noted our cloud KMS policy needs a small permission bump to `cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt`. Is HSM required?

anika: Not for initial rollout; the signer supports software-wrapped keys but the security team prefers key-wrap via KMS + CMEK. Ops will toggle HSM later.

maria: Two quick asks: 1) audit logging — we need to ensure all signing events and RBAC changes are captured and forwarded to Splunk/retained 365d. 2) vuln triage: the rebuild should pick the patched libc but we need a mechanism to stop rollout if new scan finds criticals.

kevin: For audit: we'll add explicit `audit-policy` entries for the `image-signer` SA and for rolebinding modifications. Example audit rule: `RequestURI contains "/apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io" || user == "system:serviceaccount:infra:image-signer"` 
Also we can add a dedicated logging sidecar that ships /var/log/signing.log to secure-splunk.

sam: On the vuln gate: propose a pre-flight job that runs Trivy/Grype on the new image and fails the canary promotion if `severity >= HIGH`. We already have `ci/image-scan:canary-check` in the pipeline.

anika: Exactly. Plan:
- build new minimal base images (distroless + musl where possible)
- static SBOM generation and upload to artifact-store
- run vulnerability scan (trivy) as part of the pre-canary pipeline
- run canary in a fenced cluster with `image-policy: canary` for 24h
- if scans or telemetry show regressions, auto-rollback policy triggers

liam: For KMS integration we need to update the signer config: 
```json
{"signer": {"kms_key": "projects/our-proj/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/signing", "wrap": "kms"}}
```
Make sure the signer service has `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` on that key.

maria: How will we coordinate on-call during the window? There were some issues last time where image signing outages caused traffic to hit fallback and caused a surge of retries.

anika: Good point. Ops-oncall will be paged if signer_latency > 500ms or errors > 2% for 5m. We'll also pre-open a release-war-room thread and a temporary redirect that lets traffic fall back to a read-only image cache (no re-sign).

kevin: RBAC rollout note: we'll stage RoleBinding creation behind a feature toggle. Do not delete old bindings until traffic is confirmed stable (48h). Also we need an audit entry that captures who approved the binding change.

sam: One more technical nit — `kubectl` command we'll use for canary binding: 
```
kubectl create rolebinding signer-canary-binding --role=image-signer-role --serviceaccount=infra:image-signer --namespace=canary
```
We should run that from a CI job with short-lived creds.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: canary-image-rebuild-2026-03-24 at 2026-03-24T03:00:00Z (initiated by anika). Build artifacts: gcr.io/redwood/images/base-minimal:20260324-canary.

liam: I'll coordinate the KMS permission grant with cloud-ops; expect a short IAM ticket and will flag when done.

maria: I'll own the vuln-scan job and the SBOM upload. I'll add the preflight step to the pipeline this afternoon.

anika: Thanks. Action items: sam = RBAC playbook + CI job for binding; liam = KMS IAM change + signer config; maria = SBOM + scans; kevin = audit-policy update + Splunk pipeline; ops = on-call coverage and fallback cache.

sam: acked.

liam: noted, will update when IAM is live.

kevin: I'll draft the audit-policy PR now.

anika: I'll open the release-war-room thread and post the runbook. If anyone spots an unexpected blocker ping me directly. :thumbsup:

maria: small follow-up: telemetry checkpoints we care about during canary: signing_latency_p50/p95, image_pull_errors, container_start_failures. I'll add dashboards.

sam: Also add a canary k8s admission webhook log filter so we can see denial reasons quickly.

anika: Perfect. We'll reconvene Mon EOD for final sign-off.

kevin: quick PS: remember to document the key rotation plan in the KMS playbook — must rotate KEK annually or on suspected compromise.

anika: noted. thanks team.
